module.title: Git, GitHub And Developer Workflow
module.description: Learn how developers save code, track changes, collaborate, and manage projects using Git and GitHub.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Git is a tool that tracks code changes and helps developers manage projects safely.

sections.heading: Why Git Exists
sections.content: Developers constantly update code. Git helps save versions so mistakes can be fixed and older versions can be restored.

sections.heading: Tracking Changes
sections.content: Git records what changed, who changed it, and when the change happened.

sections.heading: Why Developers Need Git
sections.content: Without Git, developers could accidentally lose important code or overwrite project files.

sections.heading: Git Works Locally
sections.content: Git runs on your computer and tracks changes inside project folders.

easyExample.title: Game Save Example
easyExample.content: Git works like game save points. If something breaks, you can return to an older saved version.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: GitHub is a website where developers store, manage, and share Git projects online.

sections.heading: Why GitHub Exists
sections.content: Git works locally on your computer, but GitHub allows projects to be stored online.

sections.heading: Collaboration
sections.content: Multiple developers can work together on the same project using GitHub.

sections.heading: Project Backup
sections.content: GitHub stores project code safely online so it is not lost if your computer fails.

sections.heading: Open Source Projects
sections.content: Many public projects on GitHub allow developers to learn, contribute, and collaborate.

easyExample.title: Google Drive Example
easyExample.content: GitHub works like Google Drive for code, but with powerful developer tracking features.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Git saves project progress using commits.

sections.heading: What Is A Commit?
sections.content: A commit is a saved checkpoint of your project at a specific moment.

sections.heading: Why Commits Matter
sections.content: Commits help developers track project history and restore previous versions.

sections.heading: Commit Messages
sections.content: Commit messages describe what changes were made.

sections.heading: Good Developer Habit
sections.content: Developers make commits regularly while building projects.

easyExample.title: Notebook Example
easyExample.content: Imagine saving your notebook after every chapter so you can return if something gets damaged.

basicCode.title: Commit Example
basicCode.code:
git add .
git commit -m "Added login page"

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Pushing uploads local code changes to GitHub.

sections.heading: What Is Push?
sections.content: Push sends local project updates from your computer to GitHub.

sections.heading: What Is Pull?
sections.content: Pull downloads latest project updates from GitHub to your computer.

sections.heading: Why Synchronization Matters
sections.content: Developers need synchronized projects while working together.

sections.heading: Team Collaboration
sections.content: Push and pull allow multiple developers to work on shared projects.

easyExample.title: Cloud Sync Example
easyExample.content: Push works like uploading files to cloud storage, while pull works like downloading latest files.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Branches allow developers to work on features separately without affecting the main project.

sections.heading: Why Branches Exist
sections.content: Developers need safe spaces to test and build features without breaking the main project.

sections.heading: Main Branch
sections.content: The main branch contains the stable version of the project.

sections.heading: Feature Branches
sections.content: Developers create separate branches for new features or bug fixes.

sections.heading: Merging
sections.content: After testing, branches can be merged back into the main project.

easyExample.title: School Project Example
easyExample.content: Different team members work on separate sections of a school project before combining everything together.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Developer workflow is the process developers follow while building and managing software projects.

sections.heading: Starting A Project
sections.content: Developers create project folders, initialize Git, and connect GitHub repositories.

sections.heading: Building Features
sections.content: Developers create branches, write code, test features, and save commits regularly.

sections.heading: Uploading Code
sections.content: Completed features are pushed to GitHub for storage and collaboration.

sections.heading: Working In Teams
sections.content: Teams review code, merge updates, and continue improving projects together.

easyExample.title: Factory Workflow Example
easyExample.content: Software development works like a factory where different people handle different tasks before combining everything into one final product.

basicCode.title: Basic Workflow Example
basicCode.code:
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial project"
git push origin main
